blocks.text: There are four animals whose wisdom Solomon, himself the wisest of kings, admires. Among them the locust has no king, ויצא חוצץ כלו, yet it goes out to war, each one dividing for itself, Prov. XXX, 27, that is, the booty and the spoils of war, which is otherwise the prerogative of kings and commanders. Thus in Exodus XV, 9 Pharaoh says, I will divide the spoils, etc. And Moses, Joshua and David divide the booty among their people. In Hebrew idiom, to go out by itself often means to go out to war. So Gen. X, 11. Out of that land he (Nimrod) went forth into Assyria, namely to make war. 2 Sam. XI, 1. At the time when kings go forth: that is, at the time when they are accustomed to set out for wars, as Jerome rightly says. Zachar. XIV, 3. The Lord went forth, he fought against the nations. Esa. XLII, 13. The Lord goes forth as a mighty soldier. Psalm. LX, 10. (var. 12.) Thou didst not go forth, O God, with our armies. So the locust, although ἀβασίλευτος [abasileutos], as the Greek translators have it here, nevertheless goes out, namely to war, חוצץ כלו, each one dividing for itself. For locusts do not wait for a commander to assign each of them a share of the booty: [col. 459] whatever part of the field they fly into, they hold it as their own, and there is no quarrel among them over the division of the booty. Hence, on the words of Isaiah, ch. XXXIII, v. 4, And your spoil shall be gathered as the gathering of the bruchus, the ancient Hebrews cited by Kimchi say: אמר להם נביא לישראל אספו שללכם אמרו לו לבוז או לחלק אמר להם אוסף [III, 278] החסיל מה אסיפת החסיל זה כל אחד ואחד לעצמו אף שללכם כל אחד ואחד לעצמו, The prophet said to the Israelites, „Gather your spoil.“ They said to him: „To plunder, or to divide?“ And he answered, „As the gathering of the bruchus.“ And what is the gathering of the bruchus? Each of them plunders for himself. So let each one of you seize his spoil for himself ^{(9)}. We render the verb חצץ to divide, because it is the same as חצה, to halve and to divide; whence חצי, half. So Job XXI, 21. The number of his months (that is, his many months) חצצו, are cut in half. There חצצו stands for חצו. A parallel passage is Psal. LV, 24. Bloody and deceitful men לא יחצו ימיהם, shall not live out half their days. Therefore, since חצה refers to the division of booty when Moses is told in Num. XXXI, 27 וחצית את המלקוח, And thou shalt divide the booty, we think that τὸ [to] חוצץ here belongs to the same sense; all the more since among the Talmudists this very verb חוצץ is used of an arbiter who divides a disputed thing between the contending parties. As in Bava Bathra ch. 8.

[III, 279] fol. 133. b. חוצצין מחיצה לזה ומחיצה לזה, They divide half to this one, and half to that one. Such arbiters are called in the Gemara דייני דחצצתא, judges of division, or of halving. In Arabic too, حصّة [ḥiṣṣa], plural حصص [ḥiṣaṣ], is a portion of a thing; and the verb حصّ [ḥaṣṣa] in the third and sixth conjugations means to share and divide with another, in the fourth to give a portion to another ^{(10)}.
